title: First-generation university student (dorm, campus job, 6 classes, morning crammer, break week) promised Dev she would finish her part of the BUS 256 group project Saturday morning; at 9 PM Dev asks once with three answers, whatever the empty Saturday calendar or the $18.86 restaurant charge seem to say.

changes.content: I promise I'll finish my part of the BUS 256 group project Saturday morning, before I go out tonight.

dev_must_notice.what: On Fri Nov 27 at 4:10 PM she promised Dev she would finish her part of the BUS 256 group project Saturday morning (m-promise); the group project final is due Thu Dec 3 at 11:59 PM (asg-bus-256-group-project-final). Saturday morning is her usual study window, 9 to 11:30 AM (m-01 and the study routine), but nothing records whether she did it: the calendar has no study block that morning, a promise is kept or broken only by her answer, and Dev has no linked to-do. It is 8:55 PM Saturday, the promise's check-in time is 9 PM.

best_fix.what: One check-in at 9 PM, one line: 'You said you'd finish your part of the BUS 256 project this morning. How did it go?' with three buttons: [Yes, I did it] [Tomorrow instead] [It didn't happen]. Nothing else on the card. A yes gets a warm line; 'tomorrow instead' (first time, so allowed) moves the promise to Sunday and offers to put a block on Sunday morning; 'didn't happen' gets an honest, gentle line and an offer of a smaller promise for Monday's window (Mon 7:30 to 9:30 AM), never a lecture.
best_fix.why: A promise is kept or broken only by her own answer. Dev has no way to know from a calendar, a charge or silence, and guessing wrong would shame someone who finished, or praise someone who did not. The check-in is the only time Dev asks, once, in her words.

must_not: mark the promise kept or broken from the calendar, Canvas, a purchase or silence: only her answer decides
mention the $18.86 restaurant charge (tx-2026-11-28-eating-out), the empty Saturday study slot or her going out tonight on the card
offer a study block tonight after the check-in
do, write or check any of the group project
send the check-in earlier than 9 PM or again after she answers
count 'no answer' as broken: an unanswered check-in is dropped after 7 days
assumptions: The promise check-in is the proactive kind promise_check at 9 PM on the day it was due (ADR 0031); Saturday morning is the promised time, so 9 PM that day is the default check.
The simulator has no to-do records, so a linked to-do is described, not planted; nothing in her data finishes or breaks the promise.
The Saturday restaurant charge is only the ordinary spending of a night out ($18.86); it is in the data to show Dev must not use it.
'Tomorrow instead' is allowed twice; this is the first time.

tempting.suggestion: offer a study block tonight after the check-in
tempting.why_wrong: she studies mornings before class and can't focus at night (m-01); the card only asks how it went
